annotation.speech2: A uniform magnetic field pointing into the page is shown as a grid of small crosses. A positive charge travels counter-clockwise around a circle of radius r centred at O. At the rightmost point of the circle the velocity arrow points straight up, tangent to the circle, and the magnetic force arrow q v cross B points straight in toward the centre, at a right angle to the velocity. Because the cross product is automatically perpendicular to the velocity, the force can only turn the particle and never change its speed; balancing the magnetic force against m v squared over r gives r equals m v over the absolute value of q times B.
The circular orbit of the charged particle.
An arrowhead on the orbit showing the particle circulates counter-clockwise.
The velocity of the particle, tangent to the circle.
The magnetic force q times v cross B, pointing from the particle in toward the centre.
A right angle marker showing the magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity.
The radius r from the centre O out to the particle.
